Job Description

The GIS Analyst supports geospatial initiatives for the University of Tennessee's Center for Local Planning (CLP) and its mission to assist Tennessee's Cities, Counties, and Development Districts with community planning, growth management, and rural preservation. Reporting to the GIS Project Manager, this position provides technical support for the design, development, testing, maintenance, and analysis of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) data and applications related to zoning, land use, growth plans, infrastructure, and other spatial data needs. The GIS Analyst contributes to project deliverables from concept to completion, producing high-quality, accurate, and timely GIS products and analysis that support university stakeholders, including coworkers, local governments, and regional partners. The position will be hybrid in accordance with the University of Tennessee's Hybrid and Remote Work Policy.

Responsibilities

GIS Analysis and Project Support

Support GIS project planning, scheduling, and execution under the direction of the GIS Project Manager and in alignment with CLP goals.
Perform spatial analysis, data processing, and geoprocessing tasks to support planning projects and deliverables.
Assist in developing project scopes, deliverables, and timelines for assigned tasks, often balancing multiple concurrent assignments.
Ensure the quality, accuracy, and timely completion of assigned GIS deliverables.
Collaborate with internal teams and external stakeholders to support project success and quality outcomes.
Prepare maps, reports, and documentation for the GIS Project Manager, Executive Director, and partner organizations.
Assist in evaluating new GIS technologies and tools that enhance planning and decision-making capacity.
Coordinate with the GIS Project Manager and OIT staff as needed to support licensing and configuration of GIS-related products and services.
Attend internal and external meetings, assisting in the assessment of project needs and supporting the development of technical solutions.
Assist in the development and delivery of training to supporting staff, students, and local government personnel in the use of GIS technologies and applications.

Collaboration with Local, Regional and State Partners

Work collaboratively with Tennessee Development Districts, city and county governments, and regional planning organizations.
Provide GIS support for zoning maps, growth plans, future land use plans, and comprehensive planning projects.
Support data sharing and collaboration among local governments, helping ensure consistent and standardized mapping practices.
Serve as a technical resource for local planning agencies, assisting them in the use and maintenance of GIS systems.
Provide training and technical support to local government users on GIS software and best practices.

Technical Support and Data Management

Support the collection, organization, analysis, and visualization of geospatial data.
Assist in maintaining and enhancing GIS databases, ensuring accuracy, security, and accessibility.
Help develop and deploy GIS applications and tools (e.g., ArcGIS Online, Story Maps, dashboards) to support local planning efforts.
Ensure adherence to GIS standards, metadata protocols, and Tennessee state mapping guidelines.
Assist in configuring and maintaining web mapping applications and visualizations.

Travel as required.

Eurofins Scientific is an international life sciences company, providing a unique range of analytical testing services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.

Job Description

Position Summary:

The Field Technician assists with routine and non-routine sampling, monitoring, and data

collection activities in support of environmental monitoring programs and client service

requests.

Field Technician responsibilities include, but are not limited, to the following:

Collects, documents, packages, and ships samples in accordance with appropriate project

specific sampling and analysis protocols.

Perform sampling of hazardous and non-hazardous environmental samples.
Assists with routine sample preparation and/or analyses, generally on site, in support of

mobile laboratory operations or screening surveys

Completes documents and is responsible for quality control of all assignments
Plan and complete daily assigned route in accordance with priorities. Notify supervisor of any

changes to plan.

Prepare and deliver sample containers/materials to various clients in support of their account.
Regularly transport, set up, utilize, troubleshoot and break down sample collection/monitoring

equipment in support of assigned projects/customer accounts.

Communicate directly with customers providing clear and accurate information concerning

their sample collection timeline and access requirements.

Communicate with supervisor and main laboratory, routinely sending timeline and

sample/project updates throughout assigned daily route.

Perform miscellaneous on-site testing when required, record all data, and complete/submit all

required sample documents.

Transport samples from the field back to the laboratory, maintaining accurate sample custody

documentation, occasionally link up with other technicians mid-route to facilitate sample transport and supply exchanges.

Drive safely and observe all traffic laws. Maintain assigned vehicle according to company expectations for cleanliness and maintenance.
Observe all OSHA safety requirements while adhering to the company health and safety policies; do not enter any confined space(s) without direct approval from upper management.
Fill out and maintain documentation/records related to field sampling activity. Document all data as required by the method performed and maintain logbook records in a complete and ethical manner
Trouble-shooting and resolution of field equipment.
Perform preventative maintenance checks on all applicable instrumentation.
Work assigned shift/hours in support of business needs maintaining flexibility to work overtime, weekends and/or holidays when requested.
Follows and enforces company health and safety policies
Must be able to follow technical instructions and guidance.
Perform other duties as required or assigned.

Role is Monday - Friday, 7am -3:30pm, with additional hours as needed.

Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent
Must have a valid driver's license and possess a clean driving record.
Ability to operate a motor vehicle
Must be able to navigate using vehicle GPS, road maps, and written directions.
Must be able to lift up to 25lbs consistently, and up to 50 lbs occasionally.
Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write
and speak in English.
Must be authorized to work in the United States without restriction or sponsorship

The Ideal Candidate Would Possess

2+ years of environmental field testing experience, ideally drinking water and wastewatersampling

As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

The benefits package offered will vary based on the employee’s full-time or part-time regular status.

Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

We embrace diversity!
Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our vision to be the Global Leader in “Testing for Life,” our mission to contribute to a healthier and safer world, and our core values, we are building a strong foundation for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Eurofins’ commitment to sustainability begins within our own companies through a shared responsibility to people and the planet. With climate change posing an imminent threat, Eurofins and its many companies recognize their duty to proactively reduce or offset the environmental impact of essential operations while also helping our clients do the same—serving as a true ESG Enabler.

Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/

Eurofins companies offer a portfolio of over 200,000 analytical methods to evaluate the safety, identity, composition, authenticity, origin, traceability and purity of biological substances and products.

Role summary:

As a Senior Data Analyst on this team, with a focus on operations and technology, you will use operational knowledge, systems, and change management skills to strengthen operational master data and the processes and governance that surround it. This is not primarily a software development or back-office analytics role — it is a business-facing, technically fluent change agent role. Success in this role requires spending significant time with operational stakeholders, understanding how work is actually performed, identifying root cause, and guiding teams through changes to systems, processes, and master data. You will frequently step into situations where the problem is not clearly defined and there is no established procedure to follow: you will investigate, form hypotheses, partner with frontline transportation operators, translate technical findings into plain language, and guide people through the changes needed to fix the issue. Data and system configuration are tools you will use to diagnose problems and inform decisions — your primary value comes from critical thinking, curiosity, and your ability to build trust and influence stakeholders, not from writing code.

The team is a change management team operating in a technical environment. We conduct strategic reviews of our transportation systems and operational unputs to find opportunities to improve the business through configuration changes and stronger governance processes. The work is process-oriented rather than strictly procedural — there often isn't a playbook, so team members are expected to investigate ambiguous problems, form hypotheses, and drive solutions independently. This is a highly customer-facing team: members regularly build relationships with operators who don't speak “technical,” translate complex concepts into operational language, and guide them through change. Whatcom Community College (WCC) is a public associate and applied baccalaureate degree granting institution with an accomplished faculty and staff who serve 7,604 students annually on its beautiful 72-acre campus in Bellingham, Washington.
